1.say: Flip the black ENTRY-BEDROOM breaker toggle to OFF inside the open gray panel. Leave all other breakers alone.
placements: black ENTRY-BEDROOM breaker toggle labeled ENTRY BEDROOM 1,2 → OFF position in left column third breaker down in gray panel (in the video: EATON 15-amp breaker with green TEST window) using fingertip on toggle
watch_for: Flipping the wrong breaker: if the entry light still works, you hit the wrong row - re-check the handwritten ENTRY BEDROOM label on the left.
Leaving the toggle half-way: if it sits in the middle, push it fully to OFF until it clicks.
1.check_yourself: The labeled breaker toggle rests in the OFF position inside the open panel with the ENTRY BEDROOM label beside it.
1.safety: Touch only that one toggle and keep fingers off the other live breakers.

2.say: Unscrew the top and bottom screws from the white double faceplate beside the white door. Lift the white rectangular faceplate straight off the two white rocker switches.
placements: top faceplate screw → out of top hole of white double rectangular faceplate on gray wall left of white door using cordless drill-driver
bottom faceplate screw → out of bottom hole of same faceplate using cordless drill-driver
white double rectangular faceplate → off the wall away from the two white rocker switches to expose metal straps
watch_for: Bit slipping and stripping the screw: if the drill spins, stop and finish with a hand screwdriver.
Prying a stuck plate: if it sticks to paint, pull straight out, do not bend it.
2.check_yourself: Two white switches are exposed on the wall with no cover and the screw holes empty.
2.safety: Keep the breaker off and touch only the outer plate and screws, never the wires behind.

3.say: Unscrew the top and bottom silver mounting screws holding the right white switch. Loosen the green ground screw to free the bare wire. Snip the two black back wires with cutters and pull the right old switch free.
placements: top silver mounting screw of right white rocker switch → out of top tab of blue double wall box to the right of the remaining left white switch using hand screwdriver
bottom silver mounting screw of same right switch → out of bottom tab of blue box using hand screwdriver
bare copper ground wire → off the green ground screw on the right switch by loosening the screw
two black wall wires → cut free from the back of the right old switch using wire cutters, leaving stubs hanging from the blue box
right white rectangular old switch body → out of the right side of the wall opening into your hand
watch_for: Working on the wrong side: if you loosen the left switch, stop - keep the left white switch mounted and work only on the right beside the door lock.
Yanking wires: if wires stretch, cut closer to the switch, do not pull hard from the wall.
3.check_yourself: One white switch remains mounted on the left beside an open blue hole on the right with loose wires hanging out.
3.safety: Confirm power is dead with a tester and touch only insulated tool handles, never bare copper ends.

4.say: Twist the green insulated switch wire to the bare copper ground wire from the wall box. Screw a yellow cone cap over them tight.
placements: green insulated ground wire of new white smart switch → twisted together with bare copper ground wire hanging from right side of blue wall box beside the remaining left white switch
yellow cone wire cap → screwed clockwise over green-to-bare twist by hand until tight
watch_for: Loose cap: if the cap pulls off with a tug, re-twist the wires and recap.
Wrong wire in cap: if a black wire is in the cap, undo it - ground is only green to bare copper.
4.check_yourself: A yellow cap joins the green switch wire to the bare ground wire hanging from the box.
4.safety: Keep the breaker off and keep that bare twist from touching other wires or the box.

5.say: Twist the white switch wire with the bundle of white neutral wires in the back of the blue box and cap them. Cap the lone blue switch wire by itself with a yellow cap.
placements: white insulated wire of new smart switch → twisted into bundle of white neutral wall wires in back of blue wall box to the right of left white switch (in the video: three white wall wires; narration calls the cap red, finished frame shows yellow)
cone wire cap, yellow in finished frame → screwed by hand over white-to-white bundle until tight
blue insulated wire of new smart switch → left unconnected, hanging beside the bundle near the right side of the box
yellow cone wire cap → screwed by hand over bare end of lone blue wire until fully covered
watch_for: A white end sticking out: if copper shows outside the cap, reopen and retwist all whites together.
Bare blue end: if copper shows on the blue wire, it must be fully covered by its own cap, not left open.
5.check_yourself: Yellow caps close the bundled white wires and the lone blue wire near the wall opening.
5.safety: Keep the breaker off and hold the white bundle away from the black ends while you twist.

6.say: Strip about half an inch off the two black wall wires. Twist the black switch wire to one black wall wire and cap it. Twist the red switch wire to the other black wall wire and cap it.
placements: two black wall wires hanging from right blue box → stripped about half an inch / about 1 cm bare using scissors/stripper
black insulated wire of new smart switch → twisted to first black wall hot/load wire in same blue box to the right of left white switch
yellow cone wire cap → screwed by hand over black-to-black twist until tight
red insulated wire of new smart switch → twisted to second black wall hot/load wire in same blue box (in the video both wall wires are black beside the door trim; yours may be black and red)
yellow cone wire cap → screwed by hand over red-to-black twist until tight
watch_for: Copper showing below cap: if you see bare wire outside the cap, untwist, trim shorter and recap.
Twists touching: if the two capped twists touch, separate them - keep black-to-black and red-to-black pairs apart.
6.check_yourself: Yellow caps join the new switch black and red wires to the black wall wires hanging from the box.
6.safety: Keep the breaker off and keep the two black twists from touching each other while you cap.

7.say: Fold the wires in and push the new white smart switch into the right side of the box. Drive the top and bottom silver screws into the box tabs. Flip the entry-bedroom breaker to ON to test.
placements: white smart-switch body with black back → pushed into right side of blue double wall box to the right of the old white left switch, buttons facing out, wires folded behind
top silver mounting screw → through top metal tab of new switch into top hole of blue box using cordless drill-driver until snug
bottom silver mounting screw → through bottom metal tab into bottom hole of blue box using cordless drill-driver until snug
black ENTRY-BEDROOM breaker toggle → ON position in panel with fingertip to test
watch_for: Pinched wires: if the switch will not push in, pull out and refold the caps flat behind it, do not force.
Crooked switch: if it sits tilted beside the left switch, loosen screws, straighten, then retighten.
7.check_yourself: A new white smart switch sits mounted beside the old white switch in the open wall box.
7.safety: Keep fingers and tools off the capped wire ends when you turn the breaker back on to test.

8.say: Set the white double faceplate over both the old left switch and the new right smart switch. Drive the screws into the top and bottom holes snug.
placements: white double rectangular faceplate → centered over left old white switch and right new white smart switch on gray wall left of white door and electronic lock
faceplate screws → into top holes of faceplate into switch tabs using hand screwdriver until snug
faceplate screws → into bottom holes of faceplate using hand screwdriver until snug
watch_for: Covering the indicator: if the green light is hidden, loosen and recenter the plate so the light shows.
Bowing plate from overtightening: if the plate bends, back each screw off a quarter-turn.
8.check_yourself: A white double faceplate covers the wall with both switches visible and a green light on at the smart switch.
8.safety: Power is back on, so touch only the plastic plate and screwdriver handle, never the terminals behind.
